newsitem.title: GERMANY: German air traffic control authority to reduce fee.
newsitem.headline: German air traffic control authority to reduce fee.

text.p: The German air traffic control authority, Deutsche Flugsicherung (DFS), said it planned to reduce fees for the third year in a row.
Airline fees for 1998 will then fall below the level of 1993, a spokesman said.
He did not state any precise figures but said an application for lower fees would be made to German transport minister Matthias Wissmann.
The spokesman said there were no current plans to privatise the authority although this had been under consideration in Bonn.

The DFS made a profit of 11.5 million marks in 1996 on revenue of 1.42 billion marks and expected to make a profit again this year, the spokesman added. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
